prompt: Why can Vitest compile `.svelte` files and resolve `#lib` imports with no setup of its own?

choices.text: `svelte-check` compiles them for it beforehand
choices.why: `svelte-check` only checks; it hands nothing to Vitest.

choices.text: It reads the project's own `vite.config.js`
choices.why: Right: Vitest is built on Vite, plugin and imports included.

choices.text: It ships its own copy of the Svelte compiler
choices.why: It uses the SvelteKit plugin the project already has.

choices.text: It asks the running dev server to compile them
choices.why: No server runs during `npm run test:unit`.

prompt: What is the difference between `vitest run` and `vitest` on its own?

choices.text: `vitest` on its own runs only the tests that failed
choices.why: It watches and reruns; it does not filter by failure.

choices.text: `vitest run` builds the planner before testing it
choices.why: No build is made for unit tests.

choices.text: `vitest run` also starts the end-to-end tests
choices.why: Those are Playwright's, run by `test:e2e`.

choices.text: `vitest run` runs once; `vitest` keeps watching
choices.why: Right: alone, it runs the tests again whenever a file is saved.

prompt: A Vitest file sits beside the file it checks, and its name ends in `.___.ts`.
Why is the test that `mondayOf('2026-10-25')` is `'2026-10-19'` worth writing?
hint: How does JavaScript number the days?

choices.text: JavaScript numbers Sunday as 0, an easy place to slip
choices.why: Right: a slip would put Sunday's sessions in the next week.

choices.text: Sunday sessions are never counted in any total
choices.why: They count, in the week they belong to.

choices.text: The 25th of October is a public holiday in the data
choices.why: Holidays play no part in the planner.

choices.text: Dates at the end of a month are parsed differently
choices.why: That is `addDays`'s test, crossing into November.

prompt: How many tests did `src/lib/week.test.ts` run?
hint: Five of them came from one `test.each`.

prompt: After `<` became `<=` in `inWeek`, which test failed?

choices.text: None, since the change was made for a good reason
choices.why: A test cannot know the reason; it knew what was true before.

choices.text: The one about Sunday ending the week
choices.why: Sunday was in the week before and still is.

choices.text: The one about the following Monday
choices.why: Right: `inWeek('2026-10-26', '2026-10-19')` became true.

choices.text: Every test in `check.test.ts` at once
choices.why: The check does not use `inWeek`.

prompt: Why is `{ date: '2026-10-21', minutes: '30' }` one of the refused rows?

choices.text: The date is in the past, which the check refuses
choices.why: The check says nothing about past dates.

choices.text: A session must name its course to pass the check
choices.why: `problemWith` checks only the date and the minutes.

choices.text: The minutes arrive as text, as lesson 18 sent them
choices.why: Right: `'30'` is a string, and only a whole number passes.

choices.text: Thirty minutes is shorter than the minimum of five
choices.why: Thirty is well above five.

prompt: What did the failing test know about the change to `inWeek`?

choices.text: What was true before, and that it no longer was
choices.why: Right: that is all a test can know, and almost always enough.

choices.text: What the change was meant to achieve
choices.why: The lesson says the test did not know that.

choices.text: Which totals in the planner it would break
choices.why: It checked `inWeek` alone, not the totals.

choices.text: Who made it, from the history in Git
choices.why: Tests do not read Git.

prompt: How many tests passed once `check.test.ts` joined `week.test.ts`?
Why is the planner's test called `planner.svelte.test.ts`?

choices.text: The name is what makes it a component test
choices.why: It tests a class, and renders nothing.

choices.text: So that Playwright runs it in a browser
choices.why: It runs in Vitest, with no browser.

choices.text: Vitest reads only names with `.svelte` in them
choices.why: `week.test.ts` ran too, without it.

choices.text: A file with runes must go through the Svelte compiler
choices.why: Right: the name sends it there, as with `planner.svelte.ts`.

prompt: Why does each test call `source()` for its data instead of sharing one object?

choices.text: Vitest runs every test in a separate browser
choices.why: These tests run in Node, with no browser.

choices.text: So that each test starts from data of its own
choices.why: Right: the second test changes its data's week.

choices.text: A `Planner` refuses data it has been given before
choices.why: Nothing in the class checks that.

choices.text: `source()` reads the file `data/planner.json`
choices.why: It returns data written in the test itself.

prompt: In the second test, what makes `planner.total` go from 135 to 60?
hint: What is `data`, and what changed in it?

choices.text: `data.week` changed, and `data` is `$state`
choices.why: Right: the planner reads its data, so the totals follow.

choices.text: A call to `refreshAll()` at the end of the test
choices.why: No load function runs here, so there is nothing to refresh.

choices.text: A new `Planner` made with the earlier week
choices.why: The test keeps the same planner throughout.

choices.text: A component that rerenders when the week changes
choices.why: There is no component anywhere in this test.

prompt: What does `render` from `svelte/server` give a test to read?

choices.text: The JavaScript the compiler wrote for it
choices.why: That was lesson 1's `compile.mjs`.

choices.text: A tree of roles and names, as `look` prints
choices.why: That is Playwright's view, not `render`'s.

choices.text: The HTML the component produced, as `body`
choices.why: Right: the test looks for text in it.

choices.text: A live component that the test can click
choices.why: Nothing is live; there is no browser.

prompt: Which of these can a test with `render` from `svelte/server` not check? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A click on a button
choices.why: Right: nothing is clicked in HTML text.

choices.text: A form being sent
choices.why: Right: that happens in a browser.

choices.text: Focus moving to an element
choices.why: Right: there is no focus without a browser.

choices.text: The text a prop produces
choices.why: It can: `90` gave `1 h 30 min`.

prompt: How many unit tests passed once `WeekTotal.test.ts` was added?
Why is `@playwright/test` installed at exactly 1.63.0?

choices.text: Vitest 5.0.5 refuses any other version of it
choices.why: The two are installed and run separately.

choices.text: It matches `look`, so it finds lesson 1's browser
choices.why: Right: nothing has to be downloaded.

choices.text: It is the only version that supports SvelteKit 3
choices.why: Playwright drives a browser; it does not know SvelteKit.

choices.text: Newer versions cannot test with JavaScript off
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

prompt: Why does the server module read `process.env.PLANNER_FILE`?

choices.text: So the planner can keep one data file per course
choices.why: There is still one file; only its name can change.

choices.text: Because `adapter-node` cannot read a relative path
choices.why: It read `data/planner.json` since lesson 15.

choices.text: So that the browser can choose which file to load
choices.why: The browser never sees the server's environment.

choices.text: So the tests' server works on a copy of the data
choices.why: Right: the sessions the tests add never reach the planner you use.

prompt: Why does `playwright.config.ts` set `reuseExistingServer: false`?
hint: What would an old server still hold?

choices.text: Reusing it would skip the CSRF check of lesson 15
choices.why: The check belongs to every build, reused or not.

choices.text: A reused server would run with JavaScript off
choices.why: JavaScript is switched off in the browser, by `test.use`.

choices.text: Playwright cannot connect to a server it did not start
choices.why: It can; the option exists to allow it.

choices.text: An old server still holds sessions added before
choices.why: Right: a fresh one starts every run from the same data.

prompt: In the test about three minutes, why is `noValidate` set on the form?

choices.text: Playwright cannot fill in a number below `min`
choices.why: It filled in 3 before `noValidate` was set.

choices.text: The browser would refuse 3 before the server saw it
choices.why: Right: switching the browser's check off tests the server's.

choices.text: `use:enhance` needs it to show the `role="alert"` message
choices.why: The message comes from `fail()`, enhanced or not.

choices.text: Without it the browser would send minutes as text
choices.why: A form field is always sent as text, either way.

prompt: What would make the two tests in the `with JavaScript off` group fail?

choices.text: Adding `use:enhance` to another form
choices.why: Enhancement leaves the form working without JavaScript.

choices.text: Renaming a course in `data/planner.json`
choices.why: The tests use a copy, and look for sessions and weeks.

choices.text: A control that only works with a click handler
choices.why: Right: with JavaScript off, nothing would answer it.

choices.text: A slower server answering in two seconds
choices.why: `expect` waits up to five seconds for the answer.

prompt: How many end-to-end tests did `npm run test:e2e` run?
hint: Two of them with JavaScript off.

prompt: Match each command with the kind of mistake it catches.
hint: One reads code, one runs pieces, one drives a browser.

pairs.right: A property that does not exist
A rule that gives the wrong week
A form that stopped working with JavaScript off

prompt: Put what `npm test` runs in the order it runs them.
trap: A type error stops the chain before the slower tests run.

prompt: Why should most of the tests be unit tests?
hint: What does each say when it fails?

choices.text: They are fast and name the line that broke
choices.why: Right: an end-to-end failure only says a journey broke somewhere.

choices.text: End-to-end tests cannot run with JavaScript off
choices.why: Two of the planner's do exactly that.

choices.text: Unit tests also check the framework itself
choices.why: The framework is Svelte's and SvelteKit's to test.

choices.text: `svelte-check` reads only unit test files
choices.why: It reads every file in `src`.

prompt:
Why do the planner's tests look for text and roles rather than `

`?
hint: What changes when a style changes?

choices.text: Classes are removed from the HTML in a build
choices.why: Scoped classes stay; they change with the styles.

choices.text: A class changes with every style and proves nothing
choices.why: Right: text and controls survive a redesign.

choices.text: Screen readers announce the class of each element
choices.why: They announce roles and names, not classes.

choices.text: Playwright cannot find an element by its class
choices.why: It can; it is just the wrong thing to ask for.

prompt: A change puts every Monday's sessions in two weeks. Which check is the quickest to catch it?
hint: It is a rule about weeks.

choices.text: `npm run test:unit`, in `week.test.ts`
choices.why: Right: that is the test that failed in this lesson.

choices.text: `npm run test:e2e`, in its JavaScript-off group
choices.why: None of those tests looks at a Monday.

choices.text: None: such a change looks plausible to every check
choices.why: It looks plausible on the page, not to the test.

choices.text: `npm run check`, since the types are wrong
choices.why: `<=` has the same types as `<`.

prompt: A component only displays text from its props. Which test suits it best?

choices.text: A Playwright test that builds and serves the planner
choices.why: That is far slower than needed for text from props.

choices.text: A test named `.svelte.test.ts` with `$state`
choices.why: That name is for tests that use runes themselves.

choices.text: A `svelte-check` run with no tests at all
choices.why: It checks types, not the text a component shows.

choices.text: A Vitest test with `render` from `svelte/server`
choices.why: Right: like `WeekTotal.test.ts`.
